subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Acromegaly and Cushing disease: IGF-1, petrosal sampling and transsphenoidal cure

steps.say: Acromegaly is suspected from enlarging hands, jaw and brow and it is screened with IGF-1 first. Growth hormone is failing to suppress below one on glucose testing. Autonomous secretion is thus proven from a somatotroph adenoma.
steps.tx: Acromegaly screening starts with **IGF-1**, and failure of growth hormone to suppress below 1 ng per mL on oral glucose tolerance testing confirms autonomous secretion from a somatotroph adenoma. A raised age-matched IGF-1 alone is never enough. Dynamic failure of suppression makes the diagnosis.

vis.alt: Medical illustration of acromegaly showing a pituitary adenoma with frontal bossing, mandibular prognathism and enlarged spade-like hand.
vis.caption: Pituitary adenoma with acromegalic face and hand prompting IGF-1 screening. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Selective adenomectomy through the nose is first choice for acromegaly. Cure is defined by normal IGF-1 with low random growth hormone. Residual disease is rechecked at three months.
steps.tx: **Transsphenoidal surgery** with selective adenomectomy is first-line for acromegaly, with surgical cure defined as normal age-matched IGF-1 plus random growth hormone below 1 ng per mL. Cure is judged at twelve weeks when swelling settles. Earlier values mislead because hormone lags behind resection.

steps.say: Persistent disease is treated with somatostatin analogues that are shrinking most tumours. Cabergoline is added for mild excess while pegvisomant is blocking the receptor. Liver tests are watched on pegvisomant.
steps.tx: Persistent disease gets somatostatin analogues such as **octreotide LAR**, cabergoline for mild cases, and pegvisomant growth hormone receptor blockade with liver monitoring for resistant tumours. Analogues also shrink tumour before reoperation. Pegvisomant normalises IGF-1 without shrinking the adenoma. Cabergoline suits patients refusing injections.

steps.say: Cushing disease is ACTH-driven cortisol excess from a corticotroph adenoma. Overnight dexamethasone is failing to suppress morning cortisol above the cutoff. Late-night salivary cortisol is confirming the excess.
steps.tx: **Cushing disease** is ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism from a corticotroph adenoma, screened with 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression showing cortisol above 1.8 mcg per dL plus late-night salivary cortisol. Two abnormal first-line tests earn referral. Cyclical disease needs repeated sampling. Pseudo-Cushing states are excluded first.

steps.say: Petrosal sinus sampling is proving pituitary source and it is lateralising the side. A basal ratio of two or more is diagnostic and stimulation is raising the bar to three. Sinus anatomy is mapped first to avoid false lateralisation.
steps.tx: Inferior **petrosal sinus sampling** with a central to peripheral ratio of 2 or more basally and 3 or more after CRH proves pituitary source and lateralises the adenoma side. Sampling is reserved for equivocal MRI with confirmed ACTH dependence. Venous variants explain most misleading lateralisation.

steps.say: Selective adenomectomy is curing most microadenomas when the surgeon is finding them. Severe hypercortisolism is bridged with steroid-blocking drugs meanwhile. Bilateral adrenalectomy with lifelong Nelson watch is the last resort.
steps.tx: **Selective adenomectomy** through the transsphenoidal route cures most microadenomas, with ketoconazole or metyrapone bridging severe hypercortisolism and bilateral adrenalectomy with lifelong Nelson surveillance as last resort. Bridging protects the patient while surgery is arranged. Nelson syndrome means the remnant corticotroph tumour grows after adrenal removal.

steps.say: Diabetes insipidus is appearing after many transsphenoidal operations, with a full three-phase course in a minority. Sodium is monitored closely through the first two weeks. A second dip around day seven is suggesting SIADH-like retention instead.
steps.tx: Postoperative diabetes insipidus with the **triphasic response** unfolding in 3 phases and SIADH-like hyponatraemia around day 7 are watched with strict sodium monitoring after every transsphenoidal operation. Thirst with dilute polyuria marks the first phase. Sodium is checked daily until stable.

steps.say: Field testing is showing outer halves lost in both eyes when the chiasm is compressed. Progressive visual loss is forcing urgent decompression. Full endocrine workup is never awaited when sight is fading.
steps.tx: Visual field testing shows **bitemporal hemianopia** from chiasmal compression, and urgent decompression is indicated for progressive visual loss even before complete endocrine workup. Quadrantanopia can precede the full hemianopia. Delay risks permanent field cuts. Acuity and colour vision are tested alongside fields.

vis.alt: Diagram of pituitary tumour compressing the optic chiasm causing bitemporal hemianopia, with acromegalic hand and facial features.
vis.caption: Chiasmal compression by pituitary tumour gives bitemporal hemianopia. Credit: StewardMD.
